wiki_catalogs.name: Project Overview
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for this section focused on the KPAH-qoder game server. Explain its purpose as a high-concurrency MMORPG backend handling up to 40,000 players. Describe the core gameplay features including player progression, combat, clans, trading, and world navigation. Document the architectural vision, technology choices, and system boundaries. Include a high-level diagram showing client-server interaction, service layers, and data flow. Provide context on how this server fits into the broader game ecosystem. Explain the role of virtual threads in managing massive concurrency. Make the content accessible to new developers while providing enough depth for technical stakeholders to understand the system's scope and capabilities.

wiki_catalogs.name: Server Lifecycle Management
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create detailed documentation for the server lifecycle management system. Explain the boot sequence starting from Server.main(), including the initialization of the ServerSocketChannel, binding to the configured port, and non-blocking I/O setup. Document the role of the run() method in accepting incoming client connections and the conditions under which connections are rejected (e.g., server in maintenance mode or player limit reached). Describe the shutdown procedure triggered by the 'baotri' command, including graceful session termination, clan data persistence via ClanManager.saveDataClan(), and JVM exit. Include a sequence diagram illustrating the full lifecycle from startup to shutdown. Provide troubleshooting guidance for common issues such as port conflicts, failed socket binding, and unresponsive shutdowns. Highlight the integration with Settings.java for configurable parameters like PORT_SERVER and MAX_PLAYER.

wiki_catalogs.name: Message Protocol
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive data model documentation for the Message class, which defines the binary protocol structure used in the KPAH game server. Explain the purpose of each field: command (opcode), ByteArrayOutputStream for writing payloads, and ByteArrayInputStream for reading incoming data. Detail how messages are constructed for both outbound (via Message(int cmd)) and inbound (via Message(byte cmd, byte[] data)) flows. Document the use of DataOutputStream and DataInputStream wrappers for primitive serialization. Provide examples of message assembly for common operations like chat, item usage, and skill casting. Include guidance on proper resource cleanup using cleanup() to prevent memory leaks. Address message validation, opcode handling, and protection against malformed payloads. Explain how the protocol supports extensibility for new message types.

wiki_catalogs.name: Character Management
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for character management in the KPAH game server. Explain how Player.java serves as the core entity representing a player's character, aggregating personal data, status, and session state. Document the role of Info.java in storing profile information such as name, level, and class, and how Location.java manages positional data within the game world. Describe the initialization process during login, state persistence, and disconnection handling. Include practical examples from the codebase showing character creation, data loading from DAOs, and synchronization with the client. Address common issues such as race conditions during login, session hijacking risks, and memory bloat from inactive player instances. Provide best practices for extending character attributes and optimizing load times.

wiki_catalogs.name: Skill Execution
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the skill execution pipeline in the combat system. Explain how player-initiated skills are received from the client, validated, and processed through the SkillService. Document the sequence from message handling in MessageHandler.onMessage to skill activation logic in SkillService, including cooldown management, MP consumption, and target validation. Detail how different skill types (offensive, defensive, support) are differentiated and executed. Include examples from the codebase showing specific skill invocation patterns, such as class-specific skills for Dau Si and Chien Binh. Address concurrency during skill execution using virtual threads and describe how race conditions are prevented during high-frequency combat scenarios. Provide guidance on extending the system with new skills and integrating them with the existing template-based model.

wiki_catalogs.name: Clan System
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the Clan System, focusing on clan creation, membership management, leadership roles, and clan-wide messaging. Explain the Clan class structure, including attributes such as clan ID, name, leader, members, and resources. Document the ClanService methods for clan registration, joining, leaving, and disbanding. Describe the message flow using ClanMessage for intra-clan communication and notifications. Include examples of clan interaction workflows, such as inviting players, promoting officers, and handling clan vs. clan events. Address data consistency between Clan and Player objects, persistence strategies via PlayerDAO, and scalability considerations for managing thousands of clans under 40,000 concurrent players. Highlight integration with chat and combat systems for clan-based activities.

wiki_catalogs.name: Equipment Management
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the equipment management subsystem. Explain how equipment slots are structured in the Inventory class, including weapon, armor, and accessory slots. Describe the ItemEquip class structure, its attributes (attack, defense, durability), and how it modifies player stats via the Point system. Include examples from InventoryService methods that handle equipment changes. Address common issues such as stat desync, invalid equipment combinations, and concurrency during equipment swaps in virtual thread environment.

Document the security mechanisms in place to prevent race conditions and rollback procedures on disconnection. Include code examples showing how TradeService handles message validation, state synchronization, and conflict resolution. Describe common failure scenarios such as network interruptions or inventory changes during trade, and how the system ensures data consistency. Provide guidance on extending the trading system for new item types or currency forms, and outline performance considerations for high-concurrency environments.

Address best practices such as avoiding excessive logging in high-frequency loops, using lazy evaluation for expensive string operations, and ensuring log messages are searchable and actionable. Provide guidance on log rotation, integration with external monitoring tools, and performance impact under high load.

wiki_catalogs.name: Technology Stack & Dependencies
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Create comprehensive content for this section focused on the technology stack of the KPAH-qoder server. Detail the use of Java 21 with virtual threads for high-performance concurrency. Explain the role of Maven for dependency management and build automation. Document all critical external libraries: HikariCP for database connection pooling, Lombok for reducing boilerplate code, JSON for data serialization, and Jansi for colored console output. Include version compatibility information, integration patterns, and configuration best practices. Provide examples of how these technologies are instantiated and used within the codebase. Address performance implications and troubleshooting common dependency-related issues such as classpath conflicts or version mismatches.

wiki_catalogs.name: Virtual Thread Concurrency Model
wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop comprehensive documentation for the virtual thread concurrency model implemented using Java 21's virtual threads. Explain how ExecutorVirtualThread.submitServer() and submitThreadSession() enable efficient handling of up to 40,000 concurrent connections by leveraging lightweight virtual threads instead of traditional platform threads. Detail the performance benefits in terms of reduced memory footprint and improved context switching efficiency. Document the integration points in Server.java where virtual threads are used for handling new clients, periodic clan updates, and session updates. Include code examples showing the creation and submission of virtual thread tasks. Address best practices for thread management in high-concurrency game servers, including monitoring active thread count via the 'thread' command. Discuss limitations and potential bottlenecks when interfacing with blocking I/O operations and database calls.

wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed architectural documentation for the Session class, which manages individual client connections in the KPAH server. Describe the lifecycle from connection establishment to disconnection, including key methods like sendKey() for handshake initialization and doSendMessage() for message dispatch. Explain how Session implements ISession interface to standardize communication contracts. Document the handling of input/output streams, connection state tracking, and thread safety considerations in a high-concurrency environment (40,000+ players). Detail error handling for network interruptions and timeout management. Provide examples of session creation during login and destruction on logout. Address security aspects such as session hijacking prevention and rate limiting to mitigate denial-of-service attacks.

wiki_catalogs.prompt: Develop detailed content for the player attribute and stat system. wiki_catalogs.name: Damage Calculation

Include performance considerations in high-load scenarios with thousands of combat events per second. Provide troubleshooting guidance for common issues like incorrect damage output or stat application bugs.

wiki_overview.content:
<blog>
# Comprehensive Project Analysis: KPAH Game Server

## 1. Project Introduction

The KPAH game server is a Java-based multiplayer online game backend system designed to handle player interactions, game mechanics, and world management for what appears to be a fantasy MMORPG. The server manages player characters, combat systems, inventory, clans, and world navigation with a focus on real-time interactions and persistent game state. The core objectives include maintaining game state consistency, handling concurrent player connections efficiently, and providing a rich gameplay experience through various game mechanics like skills, equipment, and social features. The target audience consists of players engaging with the KPAH game world, with the server supporting up to 40,000 concurrent players as configured in the settings.

## 2. Technical Architecture

The KPAH server follows a modular, layered architecture with clear separation of concerns between networking, business logic, data management, and game mechanics. The system employs a virtual thread-based concurrency model for handling multiple client connections efficiently, leveraging Java 21's virtual threads through the ExecutorVirtualThread class. The architecture centers around a main Server class that initializes the game world, manages client connections, and coordinates various game systems.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Client] --> B[Network Layer]
    B --> C[Message Handler]
    C --> D[Service Layer]
    D --> E[Business Logic]
    E --> F[Data Access]
    F --> G[(Database)]
    E --> H[Game World]
    H --> I[Maps]
    H --> J[Players]
    H --> K[Monsters]
    H --> L[Items]
```

The system follows a request-response pattern where client messages are processed through a centralized MessageHandler that routes commands to appropriate service classes. Each service handles specific game domains such as combat, inventory, clans, and trading. The architecture incorporates a template-based design pattern for game entities, where templates define the properties of items, monsters, and skills that are then instantiated as needed.

## 3. Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- [Server.java](src/main/java/server/Server.java)

### Core Modules
- [Manager.java](src/main/java/manager/Manager.java)
- [MessageHandler.java](src/main/java/network/MessageHandler.java)
- [Service.java](src/main/java/services/Service.java)
- [Player.java](src/main/java/player/Player.java)
- [Map.java](src/main/java/map/Map.java)

### Configuration Approach
- [Settings.java](src/main/java/manager/Settings.java)
- [pom.xml](pom.xml)

### External Dependencies
- [pom.xml](pom.xml)

### Integration Points
- [HikariCP.java](src/main/java/database/HikariCP.java)

The server's main entry point is the Server class, which initializes the game world and starts listening for client connections on port 19129. The Manager class serves as the central repository for game data, loading templates for items, monsters, maps, and other game entities from the database during initialization. The MessageHandler processes incoming client commands, routing them to appropriate service classes that implement the game's business logic.

```mermaid
graph TD
    A[Server] --> B[Client Connections]
    A --> C[Manager Initialization]
    C --> D[Load Templates]
    D --> E[Items]
    D --> F[Monsters]
    D --> G[Maps]
    D --> H[Skills]
    B --> I[MessageHandler]
    I --> J[Service Layer]
    J --> K[ClanService]
    J --> L[InventoryService]
    J --> M[SkillService]
    J --> N[MapService]
    K --> O[ClanManager]
    L --> P[PlayerDAO]
    M --> Q[SkillBuff]
    N --> R[Map]
```

The system uses a combination of in-memory data structures and database persistence, with the HikariCP connection pool managing database interactions. Game state changes are periodically persisted to the database, with player data updated every 5 minutes as configured in the Settings class.

## 4. Key Features

The KPAH server implements a comprehensive set of MMORPG features including player character management, combat systems, inventory and equipment, social features like clans and parties, and world navigation. The game supports multiple character classes with distinct skill trees, equipment with durability and attributes, and a clan system with leadership roles and clan-specific chat.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> ServerInitialization
    ServerInitialization --> LoadingTemplates: Load from DB
    LoadingTemplates --> ReadyForConnections: Complete
    ReadyForConnections --> ClientConnected: New Connection
    ClientConnected --> Authentication: Login Process
    Authentication --> CharacterSelection: Successful Login
    CharacterSelection --> InGame: Selected Character
    InGame --> Combat: Attack Command
    InGame --> InventoryManagement: Use Item
    InGame --> SocialInteraction: Clan Chat
    InGame --> WorldNavigation: Change Map
    Combat --> InGame: Combat Complete
    InventoryManagement --> InGame: Item Used
    SocialInteraction --> InGame: Message Sent
    WorldNavigation --> InGame: Map Changed
    InGame --> Disconnected: Logout
    Disconnected --> ReadyForConnections: Available
```

The combat system supports both player-versus-monster and player-versus-player combat with various skill types and damage calculations that consider player attributes, equipment, and buffs. The inventory system manages multiple item types including equipment, potions, gems, and quest items, with mechanics for equipping, using, and trading items. The social system includes clans with leadership hierarchies, clan chat, and clan-specific activities, as well as party systems for cooperative gameplay.

- [Service.java](src/main/java/services/Service.java)
- [Player.java](src/main/java/player/Player.java)
- [Map.java](src/main/java/map/Map.java)
- [Settings.java](src/main/java/manager/Settings.java)
- [pom.xml](pom.xml)
- [HikariCP.java](src/main/java/database/HikariCP.java)
</blog>
